messages:
Anya: quick thought — we keep debating 429 vs 503 for overloaded queues. Should we prefer conservative fallback (503 to client, router retries or fallback) or proactive eviction (drop specific keys from queue to protect overall latency)?

Sam: short answer: both have tradeoffs. 429 signals client to retry (good for polite clients) but we lose chance to do soft-queueing and preserve tail latency for high-priority work. 503 is more black-and-white and easier to reason about at infra level. :thinking:

Leo: concrete example: org A bursts 2k reqs/s for 30s using a single API key. If we accept all and queue, p99 explodes for everyone. If we reject early for that key, others stay healthy. So per-key burst control + eviction seems attractive.

Ben: agree. The kicker is UX — product teams expect a single consistent error type. If we evict per-key, clients see intermittent 503s for some keys and normal responses for others which is confusing unless we document.

Anya: what about a hybrid: early precheck returns 429 for global precheck throttle, but when queues start growing we proactively evict by key (emit 503 + reason header: X-Redwood-Shed:evicted). That way polite clients retry fast when they see 429, and 503+header indicates server-side shedding.

Maria: love the header idea. We should also emit events so Console can show "evicted_by_key" vs "global_reject" in the request timeline. Ops needs to correlate evictions with per-org cost / tokens.

Sam: sketch of an enforcement policy (pseudo):
```json
{
  "global_max_inflight": 10000,
  "per_org_burst_tokens": {
    "window_sec": 60,
    "tokens": 1000
  },
  "eviction_order": ["expired_burst", "least_recent","highest_cost"]
}
```
This lets us precheck, then accept into a soft-queue up to global_max_inflight, and when we exceed, evict according to eviction_order.

Leo: telemetry we need: queued_length_by_router, evictions/sec (by reason), rejection_rate_429, rejection_rate_503, per-key_burst_tokens_remaining. Also token-cost histograms per request to preferentially evict expensive requests.

Ben: dashboard UX: add a per-org row in the Quotas dashboard showing burst_credit, queued_count, recent_evictions, and a sparkline of p50/p95 latency. Allow filtering by model and route.

Anya: we should also think about rollout safety: feature flag "proactive-eviction-v1" with sampling and a kill-switch. Start at 1% of traffic (random keyed by org id), then 5%, 25% etc. If evictions spike errors in client telemetry or increase downstream retries above threshold, rollback.

Maria: propose A/B: Group A uses conservative-fallback (current behavior: precheck -> 429 or immediate reject), Group B uses hybrid with per-key eviction + header. Compare p99 latency for non-bursting customers, error surface for bursting ones, and overall token cost.

Sam: decision checklist for rollout:
- implementation: router accepts soft-queue + eviction logic (Sam)
- telemetry: metrics & events (Leo)
- console: add dashboard panels and event view (Ben)
- docs & SDK: document 429 vs 503 behavior + header and recommended retry/backoff (Maria)

Ben: small note on client guidance: recommend exponential backoff with jitter for 429, but for 503+X-Redwood-Shed:evicted treat as a backoff hint and include X-Redwood-Reset (seconds) so clients can avoid hot looping.

Anya: ops signals to watch in canary: increase in downstream retries, increase in p95 CPU on inference nodes (if eviction causes retry storm), and percent of requests containing X-Redwood-Shed header.

infra-bot: schedule: canary deploy window requested by @Sam for 2026-10-03T16:00Z (flag=proactive-eviction-v1, sample=1%).

Leo: for telemetry shape, add a tag to traces: shed.reason={evicted_by_key,global_precheck,burst_credit_exhausted}. That makes it easy to build panels.

Sam: I'll prototype the router change this week. Plan: implement eviction priority queue keyed by org, use token cost estimator to compute eviction score, emit shed.reason and X-Redwood-Reset header.

Maria: I'll draft docs + SDK helpers to parse headers and expose a Retry-After helper.

Ben: I'll add the dashboard rows and wire up alerts: alert when evictions/sec > 50 and p99_latency_non_burst_customers > 200ms.

Anya: sounds good. If anyone is blocked on metrics we need a quick wire-up: event name = "request_shed", fields = [org_id, key_id, reason, cost_estimate, reset_secs]. Keep it lightweight.

Sam: assigned tasks in comments. I'll push a PR and ping channel when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Leo: one last thought — keep the UX in Console explicit: show "Your requests were shed due to burst protection" with a link to docs, otherwise support tickets will spike.

Ben: totally. Will add a tooltip and a query to find recent orgs with many evictions for CS to triage.

Maria: cc @ops for runbook updates.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled for canary window. Monitoring alerts configured at low sensitivity for first 24h.
